title: Sitting With It
logline: Every morning before the village wakes, a forest monk walks to the cemetery at its edge and simply sits there, the way he has for years, doing nothing that looks like very much.
human_question: What changes in a person who deliberately keeps death close, on purpose, every single day?

premise.story: A forest monk's regular practice of sitting at a village cemetery or charnel ground as part of his own training, followed over several mornings.
premise.place: A forest hermitage beside a rural cemetery.
premise.experience: Dawn light through trees, the ordinary business of a cemetery, a monk sitting still among it, and, if he chooses to speak, his own account of why.

concept_links.why: The source's own instruction is to go to charnel grounds and forests to see the dead and wisely recollect that death is certain for oneself and for everyone [C092-P4:L80-L84]. A monk who does exactly this, as an ordinary part of his life, needs no further explanation.

what_camera_could_observe: The walk from hermitage to cemetery at dawn
The monk sitting still for an extended period
The monk's own words, if he offers them, about why he comes
what_must_be_real: A real, ongoing practice by a monk willing to have it observed. The film does not claim he has attained anything; it only shows what he does.

possible_arc.opening: A dawn walk from hermitage to cemetery.
possible_arc.turn: An ordinary event at the cemetery, a caretaker at work, perhaps a funeral in the distance, met by the same stillness.
possible_arc.ending_open: The monk gets up and walks back. Whatever this practice has done to him is not something the camera can show directly.

position_hint: closing candidate: a quiet, accepting note on which to hand the group's question on toward what comes after grief, without resolving it into doctrine

requirements: A forest hermitage with an established practice of this kind near a working cemetery
A monk willing to be filmed and, if he chooses, to speak about the practice

suggestions.name: A forest hermitage in the North Central or North Western dry-zone forest belt
suggestions.region: North Central Province or North Western Province
suggestions.why: Dry-zone forest hermitages of this kind are established in this belt; no specific hermitage identified.

risks: Presenting the monk as having 'attained' something the camera cannot verify
Treating a working cemetery and grieving families nearby as scenery
drop_if: No monk with this established practice will allow filming
The nearby cemetery's use by grieving families cannot be respected during filming

connections.note: A monk who spends his working life at other people's deathbeds finds a natural route into this, his own private practice of recollecting death.
A companion piece: one watches a solitary practitioner train attention toward death, the other watches many people training attention toward stillness together.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
